dedupe_keys.name: vieques puerto rico solar battery and green hydrogen microgrid led by cornell university

description: This Cornell Chronicle article of 2 April 2026 reports on a microgrid on Vieques, an island off Puerto Rico's main island, led by Professor Hector Abruna of Cornell University with the battery maker Viridi and the local groups Community Through Colors and La Finca de Hamberto. The first mobile solar-charged battery arrived in late 2025 and now powers refrigerated food storage trucks and backs up the fire station, a clinic and the community centre, which lets the community keep medicines and food. A second battery was due in May 2026 and a green hydrogen fuel cell in early 2027, and the project expects to cut electricity costs from 30 to 33 cents per kilowatt-hour to about 15 cents. The page is free to read and states no licence. Coverage is one island and results are early. The source is a web page available online. Caveats: capacities are only described loosely, and no operating data or models are published on the page. For simulation, it is a demonstration case for resilience and capacity planning of island microgrids with hydrogen storage.
